Theme

Latin word

spatium

spatium, spatiī n.

noun, second declension

distance, space; a stretch of road or time; lap; a space, room; a space of time, a period; space, room; the distance between

In this lexicon

  • distance

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.43.1: aequum ferē spatium … aberat; Ov. M. 8.794: viae spatium, the length of the way (Lewis & Short); Traupman 203, 305; Traupman 203

  • lap

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.28: duōbus spatiīs tribusve factīs, after two or three turns (Lewis & Short); Traupman 51

  • parking space

    also used · classical · Andresian p. 41

  • period

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Arch. 1: spatium praeteritī temporis (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 6.18 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 88, 359; Traupman 30: tertiō spatiō, in the third period (class period); spatium studiōsum, study period

  • space

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BC 3.92.1: tantum erat relictum spatiī; Lucr. 1.426: locus ac spatium, quod ināne vocāmus

  • spatium cosmicum: space

    modern

  • studiōrum spatium: term

    modern

  • Hic locus aequum ferē spatium ā castrīs Ariovistī et Caesaris aberat.

    This place was about the same distance from the camps of Ariovistus and of Caesar.Caes. B.G. 1.43.1
